**Only 23% of consumers trust AI agents to handle their payments**

*The gap between agentic payments momentum among industry players and the consumer confidence needed to sustain it is widening, according to new Visa research.*

Despite rapid investment by card networks, banks and fintechs in agentic payment infrastructure, only 23% of US consumers say they trust generative AI to handle payment transactions on their behalf, according to research published by Visa. Consumers are increasingly comfortable using AI tools earlier in the shopping journey but balk at delegating the moment money actually moves.

The finding lands as the industry accelerates buildout. EMVCo drafted a card-based agentic payments framework in September, Visa and Mastercard both joined an agentic payments alliance with more than 25 founding members in August, and multiple European banks have completed pilot agentic transactions this year. Infrastructure is running well ahead of demand.

The research underlines that technical capability is a necessary but insufficient condition for consumer adoption. Authentication, transparency and consumer control will determine whether agentic payments move beyond proofs of concept. The trust deficit is not a branding problem; it reflects genuine consumer uncertainty about delegating financial authority to autonomous software.

*Sources: [Consumer trust in agentic payments continues to lag](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48369/consumer-trust-in-agentic-payments-continues-to-lag?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

stories.original:
**Meta launches AI assistant with Stripe-powered checkout capabilities**

*The rollout of Muse, a personal AI agent capable of completing purchases via Stripe, brings agentic commerce directly to a consumer audience numbering in the billions.*

Meta has launched Muse, a personal AI assistant capable of performing tasks including product discovery, checkout and payments, with Stripe providing the underlying payment processing. The agent can act across Meta's platform ecosystem, turning conversational interactions into completed transactions.

The launch represents a concrete step beyond the pilot-stage agentic payments that European banks and card networks have been testing. Where industry experiments have focused on B2B use cases or controlled merchant environments, Meta's move brings agentic commerce directly to a consumer audience numbering in the billions. Stripe's role as the payment layer reinforces its positioning as infrastructure provider for AI-native commerce, following its earlier acquisition of AI gateway OpenRouter and its partnership with AWS to build payment layers for AI agents.

European payments firms face a familiar platform dynamic. Meta and Stripe are building the rails on which agentic commerce will run, potentially marginalising local payment methods unless schemes such as Wero or open banking providers can integrate into these agent-driven flows.

*Sources: [Meta rolls out personal AI assistant Muse, with support from Stripe](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48367/meta-rolls-out-personal-ai-assistant-muse-with-support-from-stripe?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

stories.original:
**Visa and Revolut complete passkey-authenticated agentic payment in France**

*A European authentication model for agentic payments could address the consumer trust gap in autonomous transactions, with a live French pilot testing passkey-based consent within existing regulatory frameworks.*

Visa and Revolut have completed what they describe as the first passkey-authenticated agentic card payment in France. The transaction used biometric passkeys rather than traditional card credentials to authorise an AI agent to make a payment, combining agentic payments with the FIDO authentication standard.

Passkeys bind authorisation to a device and a biometric, giving consumers a visible control mechanism even when an AI agent initiates the transaction. That directly addresses the trust deficit identified in Visa's own consumer research, which found only 23% of US consumers willing to let AI handle payments. A European deployment also puts the experiment within the scope of PSD2's strong customer authentication requirements, testing whether passkey-based consent satisfies regulatory standards for agentic payments.

Revolut's involvement extends its pattern of early adoption in new payment categories. For the broader European market, the pilot offers a template for how agentic payments might work within existing regulatory frameworks rather than requiring new ones.

*Sources: [Visa and Revolut carry out passkey-based agentic payment in France](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48364/visa-and-revolut-carry-out-passkey-based-agentic-payment-in-france?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Innovate Finance calls for faster UK action on open finance and AI policy**

*The trade body's report argues the UK risks falling behind on open finance implementation and urges the government to accelerate its existing commitments.*

Innovate Finance has published a report calling on the UK government to move more quickly on open finance policy and to align its approach with the growing role of AI in financial services. The trade body positions open finance as foundational infrastructure for trusted AI applications in areas such as lending, advice and fraud prevention, and warns that delays risk ceding competitive ground to jurisdictions moving faster.

The report arrives as HM Treasury consults on modernising UK payments and open banking rules, and follows the FCA's publication of an open finance roadmap earlier this year with a 2030 target. Innovate Finance's argument is essentially that the existing policy direction is right but the pace is too slow, particularly given how quickly AI capabilities are advancing. The trade body calls for open finance to be accelerated within 2026 rather than treated as a multi-year aspiration.

The intervention reflects a broader tension in UK fintech policy. The regulatory architecture for open banking is well established, but extending it to pensions, insurance and investment data requires legislative action and cross-regulator coordination that has been slower than the industry wants.

*Sources: [Innovate Finance Urges UK Action on Open Finance and AI to Secure FinTech Lead](https://ffnews.com/news/news-innovate-finance-calls-for-faster-action-on-policy-to-keep-pace-with-fintec-22dcdd17) — Ffnews | [Innovate Finance report calls for government action to unlock UK fintech growth](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/innovate-finance-report-calls-for-government-action-to-unlock-uk-fintech-growth/) — Openbankingexpo*
